_comment: THE AGENT-SKILL LITERATURE, staged as a top-level directory ahead of becoming its own repository — the same arrangement as who-iris/, who-style-guide/, folio-assistant-sci/ and folio-assistant-core/. It holds the corpus of published guidance on authoring and operating agent skills, and the voices read out of it. ONE instance rather than the who-iris/who-style-guide pair, and the reason is the corpus: that pair is split because IRIS is a catalogue of a million items from which three were read, so the corpus and the reading have genuinely different scopes. Here the corpus IS the subject — every document in it exists to be read into these voices — so splitting would put two directories in two repositories with a one-to-one relation between them. Same shape as folio-assistant-sci, which holds `library/milnorlink` and is where the `milnor` voice is going. THIS IS NOT PLATFORM CONTENT: `AGENTS.md` opens by saying folio-assistant is the platform and not the content, and vendor documentation about skill authoring is somebody else's writing, so it does not go in cat-harness even though it is ABOUT the harness's own subject.

Carries the two rules a corpus of other publishers' documents needs and the README does not state as instructions: never edit a captured document, and say which KIND you are reading — an assertion is a convention, evidence is a finding, and nothing in the schema can tell them apart.

directories.description: The ingested corpus — one `<bib-slug>/` per document, holding `sections/*.md` and `structure.json`. THREE PUBLISHERS AND TWO KINDS, and the distinction is load-bearing rather than bibliographic: the vendor documentation is ASSERTION (a publisher describing its own product, revisable without notice and in one case describing a product that no longer exists), while the arXiv papers are EVIDENCE (a measurement somebody else can repeat). A voice rule derived from the first is a convention; one derived from the second is a finding. Nothing in the schema can tell them apart, which is why each document's `structure.json` carries its publisher and why the voices state which kind they are reading.

`folio-voice/v1` profiles read out of `library/` above — a shared base plus one override per vendor, on the owner's ruling of 2026-09-20: 'for model specific sources, make those model specific voices.' Citations are INTERNAL to this instance (no `instance:` key), unlike who-style-guide's, because here the corpus and the reading live together. The rules are deliberately NOT formally constrained: owner, same day, 'preference leave unstructured schema, agentic review b/c of best practice drift, not formal' — published best practice is revised without notice, so a schema gate would pin whichever vintage was current when it was written and then report clean over the drift.
